about: Width gate: box variants and which entries they draw. Read by tools/windows.py (marker.py, lint.py). px = line budget in px of the variant's font (big = enfont VWF, small = ensmall); "jp" = the JP's own cell width (16 px a JP char big, 8 small; pad strings: pad chars). lines 0 = the JP's own line count. last_px = budget of a page's last line (dialogue: wait orb); row_px = budget per row of the box (row 2+ uses the last). status measured = a stress line exactly px wide was seen whole in the named shot. Renderer map from tools/debug/drawcalls.lua (work/qa/dc/drawmap.tsv).

dialogue.last_note: the page-wait orb is drawn at x 226.. over the second row (work/qa/tort/orb.png): the last line of each page ends by x 224
dialogue.note: x 8..232, 224 px line whole with 3 px to the frame; VWF auto-wraps past 232; {0010} = new page

window.note: battle quotes and messages; newline = \n (0x81AD). Row 1 shows 224 px whole but row 2 drops a glyph ending past x 228 (work/qa/wg3/z.png); 220 px shows whole on both rows

battle_2row.row_note: row 2 continues in the tiles after row 1: 224 + 208 px (27 cells) shows clean, 224 + 224 overruns into the battle BG tiles (work/qa/wg6/tutorial_battle/scene.png)
battle_2row.note: tutorial prompts (and quote 135760); newline = \n, else split at 224 px; row 2 rest dropped

areas.note: map-menu area name: the drawer stops after 28 characters (224 px and 160 px stress lines both cut after char 28: work/qa/wg1/map-c.png, wg2/map-c.png)

obj_cells.note: each label owns one 16 px cell per JP char of OBJ tiles; the next label's tiles follow, so the JP cell width is the hard cap

weapon_name.note: a 208 px stress name shows whole to x 232 (the skill's tiles start 16 cells later). Also the first row of the code-built battle message 0x0810638E (see str_battle_msgs 40E534 notes)

skill_name.note: a 176 px stress name shows whole to x 232. Also row 2 of the battle message 0x0810638E after 40E534

technique_name.note: 8 cells each: the next row's label tiles follow (0x38 + 0x20 = 0x58), 128 px stress names show whole. techniques_b's battle super-move cut-in reads a JP copy of its table (build.py JP_COPIES), so translating it is safe

ability_rows.renderer: 0x08014098 VWF, shikigami page 2 (OBJ tile 0x58, 28 cells = 2 rows of 14)
ability_rows.note: the JP pads row 1 to 14 chars with fullwidth spaces; English uses \n (line plotter: x to the next multiple of 224). 224+224 and 120+224 stress rows show whole (work/qa/nl3a, nl3b)

speaker_tag.note: dialogue speaker plate: a 40 px stress name shows whole, x 12..50 inside the frame's x 10..53, centred by pixels; ROM table names, player name and shikigami names (RAM halfwords) all go through `plate` (work/qa/sp3/plates.png)

small_label.note: battle BG labels, all 10 callers read: 40F718/24/30 at tile dests 0x0600CC80/CD00/CD80 (0x80 apart = 4 tiles = the JP's 32 px, 0x0810C1CE..); 410C0C (x 0) and 410C80 (x 27, 3 tiles to the screen edge) share dest 0x06009800. The JP's tile count is the hard cap

intro_strip.note: line drawn from x 8; a 240 px stress line is cut after x 232 (28 cells x 8 px)

credits.note: line drawn from x 0; a 240 px stress line shows whole to x 239 (30 cells x 8 px). Centre with leading spaces

name_grid.renderer: 0x0803AEB2 -> gridline (one centred glyph per 16 px cell)
name_grid.note: name-entry character grid rows: glyph sets the cursor picks from by index, not text. The ABC tab's fullwidth letters are the English font's letters, drawn one per cell (scene name_entry_abc); kana tabs unchanged

name_field.note: default player name: copied to RAM as 5 halfwords (vwf.py, was 2), so at most 4 letters + NUL; the field has 5 cells before the grid's tiles

name_title.note: the small label 40C530's tiles start right after the title's 4 cells (0x06008220): a 75 px title showed the label's tiles in its 5th cell (work/qa/ne6/both.png)

link_window.note: link-cable (2-player) rules / continue / waiting messages: only shown with a link partner, so not reachable in one emulator. Window budget assumed; JP rows padded with spaces, English uses \n

unused.note: str_battle_help: its only reader 0x0800F010 has no caller and no pointer to it (dead; test filler '１２３４５６７８９０'); str_debug_menu: a leftover graphics-viewer menu (table 0x08125E68, code 0x0800C8A8..) not reached in normal play. Kept Japanese (docs/decisions.md D9)

data_keys.note: str_battle_kanji: 257 one-kanji strings behind table 0x0840E56C, read only by 0x08109614, which matches each kanji of a techniques_b name to pick the super-move cut-in graphic. Never displayed as text; translating them would break the cut-in
